terms.comment: A description. We have found no set term in Lewis & Short, Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Roman streets had names (vīcus Tuscus, vīcus Scelerātus, Sacra Via), and Latin says what a street is called with vocant or appellant, as Livy does, or with the dative and nōmen est, as Cicero says of a spring: Quid huic viae nōmen est?

phrases.latin: Quid huic viae nōmen est? — Via Nova.
phrases.english: What’s this street called? — New Street.

phrases.latin: Hīs locus ad habitandum datus quem deinde Tuscum vīcum appellārunt.
phrases.english: They were given a quarter to live in, which was afterwards called Tuscan Street.
and the place is a reminder of it: they call it Wicked Street

phrases.latin: In hāc īnsulā extrēmā est fōns aquae dulcis, cui nōmen Arethūsa est
phrases.english: at the tip of this island there is a spring of fresh water called Arethusa
